https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: See what the new skink character can do in your games of Warhammer Age of Sigmar.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
Yesterday, we saw how interpretations of the Great Plan are central to your new Seraphon army rules, but if you’re going to build your war host around them, you’ll need to know what your warriors do. Luckily, the prophets have granted us a peek at future warscrolls, so let’s see what they say.

Blessed Tetaxi

As the new skink on the block, Blessed Tetaxi is a good place to start. The Prophet of Tepok sits astride a mighty flying monster and channels the will of his god to predict which enemies carry dark omens – choosing one enemy unit within 12” in each of your Hero Phases. Tetaxi can invoke the Stone of Tehemundi to flood a foe’s mind with cosmic revelations, and if they’re his dark omen that turn, it’s even easier to slay one of their models outright.

Your Hero Phase

DARK OMENS

Tetaxi’s mind is filled with visions of a coming Dark Day. When his visions clears, he hyper-focuses on one enemy, singling them out as the most pressing target of the moment.

Declare: Pick a visible enemy unit within 12" of this unit to be the target.

Effect: The target is a dark omen for the rest of the turn.

Your Hero Phase

THE STONE OF TEHEMUNDI (4)

Focusing upon the ovoid artefact he believes was gifted to him by Tepok, Tetaxi projects his visions into the minds of others. Few are able to withstand such an onslaught of cosmic truths.

Declare: Pick a visible enemy unit within 18" of this unit to be the target, then make a chanting roll of D6.

Effect: Roll a dice. If the target is a dark omen or the chanting roll was 8+, roll 2D6 instead. If the roll exceeds the target’s Health characteristic, 1 model in the target unit is slain.

KEYWORDS: PRAYER

You can also invoke an asterism* if the dark omen dies that turn, effectively adding an extra source of divine inspiration to your army rule.

Once Per Battle, End of Your Turn
TEPOK’S WILL

Guided by visions he believes are sent by Tepok, Tetaxi comes up with his own interpretations of the Great Plan. He is only tolerated by the slann as his predictions appear to be coming true.

Effect: If an enemy dark omen was destroyed this turn, pick 1 of the following asterisms to witness: ‘Coils of Sotek’, ‘Rays of Chotec’, ‘Jaws of Itzl’ or ‘Eye of Tepok’.

Kroxigor Warspawned

Need a way to ensure Tetaxi’s target shuffles off their mortal coil that turn? Bring some Kroxigor Warspawned to the party, whose weapons now hit for 3 and 4 Damage without needing an attendant skink unit nearby, while gaining an extra attack when charging or wrestling over an objective.

Aggradon Lancers

Charging headlong into combat is great fun, and if anyone loves it more than kroxigors, it’s the Aggradon Lancers. They’re now more geared towards tearing through Infantry than shearing Monster hides, dealing mortal damage after charging and steadily healing to keep them in the fight for longer.

Engine of the Gods

We can’t have a skim through Seraphon warscrolls without seeing a massive reptilian beast, and the Engine of the Gods is one of the most impressive. It still serves as a locus for regenerating your fallen warriors – now drawing energy from nearby Priests to channel restorative magics – but gains a new role as a powerful centrepiece of support abilities, using asterisms you’ve beheld to enhance other Seraphon.

ENGINE OF THE GODS

Once Per Turn (Army), End of Any Turn

STARLIGHT SUMMONS

Memories of fallen Seraphon warriors coalesce from pure Azyrite magic into new physical forms.

Declare: Pick up to 3 visible friendly SERAPHON PRIESTS wholly within 12" of this unit to be the targets.

Effect: Remove any number of ritual points from the targets and give them to this unit. This unit can have a maximum of 6 ritual points. Then, pick a friendly SERAPHON unit wholly within 12" of this unit and return a number of slain models to it with a combined Health characteristic of up to the number of ritual points this unit has. Then, remove a number of ritual points from this unit equal to the combined Health characteristic of the models returned by this ability.

KEYWORDS: RAMPAGE

Passive

COSMIC ENGINE

The Engine of the Gods is a mysterious device capable of altering the natural laws of the universe.

Effect: For each of the following asterisms you have witnessed, apply the corresponding effect to friendly SERAPHON units while they are wholly within 12" of this unit:

Coils of Sotek: Add 3 to the control scores of those units.

Rays of Chotec: Add 1 to run rolls for those units.

Jaws of Itzl: Add 1 to wound rolls for combat attacks made by those units while they have not charged in the same turn.

Eye of Tepok: Add 1 to unbinding rolls for those units.

Battletome: Seraphon goes up for pre-order on Saturday alongside the Blessed Tetaxi miniature. In the meantime, join us later in the week as we take a look at the new Armies of Renown.

* As per the Great Plan, we talked about asterisms yesterday.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Blood for the Blood God! Plus, authors, a quiz, and a bitter rivalry reignited on Battle Report.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
This week on Warhammer TV, The Butcher’s Nails makes its blood-soaked debut, fan-favourite author Chris Wraight chats about writing, and Battle Report hosts an Age of Darkness grudge match.

Available Friday: Hammer and Bolter – The Butcher’s Nails

The World Eaters are drawn to the far-flung rocky moon of Lamens by an ancient prophecy. As they launch their brutal attack… No, sorry, you’ll just have to wait until Friday to see what happens! We’ll have a full article dedicated to the blood-drenched Warhammer 40,000 animation when it launches.

We know you can feel the nails humming in your skull, but while you wait, you can enjoy these shows.

Available now: Scribes and Scriveners – Chris Wraight

From Warhammer Fantasy to the Vaults of Terra and The Scouring, few authors have had such a wide sweeping journey across the worlds of Warhammer as Chris Wraight. He joins host Alex on this week’s Scribes and Scriveners to talk about his extensive back catalogue, and to answer that crucial question for all authors – does he plan everything meticulously in advance?

Chris chats about his approach to writing and how easy it can be to become overwhelmed in the whole writing process. Watch now to enjoy a unique insight into the creative process of one of Black Library’s most prolific authors.

Available tomorrow: Brainboyz – Ork Speshul

Fink you’ve got a head full of Orky know-wots? Test your knowledge in a special edition of Brainboyz focusing entirely on the most brutal (and kunnin’) of the Warhammer 40,000 factions – the Orks.

If you know your Trukks from your Traktor Kannons, or think you can spot an Attack Squig from a thousand paces, why not tune in and see how you fare against our contestants in this noggin’ scratching quiz show. 

Available Thursday: Battle Report – Warhammer: The Horus Heresy


This week, Battle Report takes us to the galaxy-spanning battlefields of The Horus Heresy, throwing two forces into the claustrophobic and chaotic maelstrom of a Zone Mortalis engagement.

Regular viewers will recognise the generals from the 2025 edition of A Tale of Four Gamers. Quinn has returned with the noble Salamanders to take on Josh, who commands the malevolent Word Bearers. Both of these forces were the ones they built, painted, and played with a year ago, so it’s a great opportunity to see what tactical lessons the two generals have learnt in the last 12 months.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Bretonnians return at full tilt for Warhammer: The Old World
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Ride out for the lady with the Army Reinforcement Set.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
The nobility of fair Bretonnia are riding out in a boxed set containing brand new plastic Knights of the Realm, Knights Errant, and Pegasus Knights for Warhammer: The Old World.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

The Kingdom of Bretonnia: Knights of Bretonnia Army Reinforcement Set is packed with 22 new plastic miniatures:

  • 6 Pegasus Knights

  • 16 Knights of the Realm (which can alternatively be built as Knights Errant)

This boxed set features updated versions of fan-favourite kits, each packed with detail and realised with dynamic posing which captures them riding into the heart of the Lady’s enemies.

Pegasus Knights

Only the richest and most influential knights can boast of owning a battle-trained pegasus, as these majestic creatures are difficult to capture and even harder to train. On the battlefield, Pegasus Knights often flock together, providing a devastating aerial threat as they range ahead of the main army in the search of honourable combat.*

The miniatures in the Army Reinforcement Set can be fielded as a unit of six Pegasus Knights or as two units of three, each with the option for a champion, standard bearer, and musician.**

Knights Errant

Young knights of Bretonnia are expected to earn their spurs and prove themselves against the foe on the field of battle. Knights Errant are eager to prove their worth, and their need to attain status and renown leads to acts of enthusiasm which can border on reckless.

This new kit contains interchangeable heads, lances, and shields, and full command options.

Knights of the Realm

Knights of the Realm make up the bulk of the nobility of Bretonnia and form the core of their fighting forces. A Knight of the Realm is duty bound to defend their people and land until death, and is expected to uphold the tenets of Bretonnian chivalry and maintain their own standards of honour.

This new kit contains interchangeable heads,*** lances, and shields, and full command options.

The 16 Knights in this boxed set can each be built as either of the above options, so you can choose to build your army around a core of experienced Knights of the Realms, launch your own errantry war with loads of Knights Errant, or create a balanced force that includes both.

The Army Reinforcement Set is a great way to build upon your existing ranks. Alternatively, if you are a fledgling knight looking to pledge your devotion to the Lady, this is an ideal starting point for a new force.

Arcane Journal: The Sacking of Reaver’s Point

Along with the boxed set comes a new Arcane Journal. The Sacking of Reaver’s Point follows the noble knights of Bretonnia as they seek to stave off the predations of Frydaal the Chainmaker and her Norscan raiding fleets. The forces of Couronne gather as the wolfships threaten the northern coasts of Bretonnia.

This Arcane Journal features new rules for the Kingdom of Bretonnia, including an Army of Infamy representing veteran defenders of the realm, new lore and scenarios, and updated rules for using Chaos Dragons in your games of Warhammer: The Old World.

We’ll have more on the Kingdoms of Bretonnia closer to their release, so keep an eye on Warhammer Community for updates. In the meantime, grab a copy of Warhammer: The Old World – Forces of Fantasy so you’ve got the rules for your Pegasus Knights, Knights Errant, and Knights of the Realm.

* They are also part of an almost impossible quest – to discover the plural of ‘Pegasus’.

** Playing a trumpet while riding a flying horse has never looked so effortless.

*** The helmets also have crest choices, including griffon, lion, unicorn, tower, and bull.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Enact the Great Plan with new Seraphon army rules
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Take a look at some of the new rules dropping with Battletome: Seraphon.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
Battletome: Seraphon is available to pre-order this weekend. The heavens have aligned to allow us a sneak peek at the upcoming army rules for everyone’s favourite cold-blooded warriors.

The Great Plan

The slann have a plan, and it’s up to Seraphon commanders to Interpret the Great Plan. There are five stages to the Great Plan, and you pick three when you build your army to form your own interpretation. Creating an army to hunt enemy Heroes? Destroy the Malefactor is probably the choice for you. Picking loads of Wizards and Priests? Awaken the Ley Lines is the way to go.

INTERPRET THE GREAT PLAN

During army composition, you must pick 3 of the following stages to form your interpretation of the Great Plan and record them on your army roster. During the battle, you will be aiming to complete these stages to receive the guidance of the Old Ones in the stars, unlocking powerful abilities for the rest of the battle.

Destroy the Malefactor: An enemy HERO has been destroyed this battle.

Restore the Astromatrix: There is a friendly SERAPHON unit wholly within 12" of each battlefield corner.

Awaken the Ley Lines: 5 or more spells cast or prayers chanted by friendly SERAPHON units, in any combination, have been successfully cast or answered this battle.

Scour the Corruption: There is a friendly SERAPHON unit contesting a terrain feature that you control, and that terrain feature is within enemy territory and not within friendly territory.

Protect the Realmshaper: It is the third battle round or later, there is a friendly Realmshaper Engine on the battlefield, and there are no enemy units within 6" of that friendly Realmshaper Engine.

Meeting the conditions of a stage of the Great Plan causes shifts in the firmament, which Seraphon forces interpret as a sign that they are on the true path. On the battlefield, these manifest as asterisms, powerful stellar alignments which can grant your army potent boons. 

You can witness one asterism for free at the start of the battle, and another for each condition of the Great Plan you meet, meaning you can easily cascade multiple asterism effects across your army. For example,  you can call on the Coils of Sotek to descend from the heavens and constrict enemy units, hampering their ability to fight.

BATTLE TRAITS

Once Per Battle Round (Army), Any Hero Phase

COILS OF SOTEK

Shimmering serpent-forms constrict the foe, hampering their assault.

Declare: You can only use this ability if you have witnessed the ‘Coils of Sotek’ asterism. Pick a friendly SERAPHON unit to be a target. If you have witnessed 3 or more asterisms, you can pick an additional friendly SERAPHON unit to be a target.

Effect: For each target, pick an enemy unit in combat with that target. For the rest of the turn, subtract 1 from the Attacks characteristic of melee weapons used by those enemy units while they are in combat with any of the targets.

KEYWORDS: ASTERISM

The Eye of Tepok is going to be a welcome sight for Seraphon players who have built their army around magic, granting a huge boost to casting or chanting rolls.

BATTLE TRAITS

Once Per Battle Round (Army), Any Hero Phase

EYE OF TEPOK

Iridescent winds swirl about the wisest of the Seraphon, enhancing their rituals and spellcasting.

Declare: You can only use this ability if you have witnessed the ‘Eye of Tepok’ asterism. Pick a friendly SERAPHON unit to be a target. If you have witnessed 3 or more asterisms, you can pick an additional friendly SERAPHON unit to be a target.

Effect: The next time each target uses a SPELL or PRAYER ability this turn, when making the casting roll or chanting roll, add 1 to the number of dice rolled, to a maximum of 3, then remove 1 dice of your choice and use the remaining dice as the roll.

KEYWORDS: ASTERISM

Spells, Prayers, and Artefacts

Speaking of Tepok, they’re likely to have their eye on the Lore of Celestial Manipulation, which introduces some new spells for Seraphon players, including Celestial Reinforcement which is perfect for when your forces are looking thin on the ground.

LORE OF CELESTIAL MANIPULATION

Your Hero Phase

CELESTIAL REINFORCEMENTS (7)

Casting their mind to a distant temple-ship or nearby temple-city, the slann summons fresh Seraphon to the battlefield in an eye-searing flash of light.

Declare: Pick a friendly SERAPHON WIZARD to cast this spell, pick a friendly non-HERO non-MONSTER SERAPHON unit that has been destroyed to be the target, then make a casting roll of 2D6. Subtract 1 from the casting roll if it is the enemy turn.

Effect: Set up a replacement unit with half the number of models from the target unit (rounding up) wholly within 12" of the caster and more than 9" from all enemy units.

KEYWORDS: SPELL

It’s worth noting that some units which were previously wizards have now had a slight career change with the latest battletome. The Skink Starseer, Skink Starpriest, and Skink Oracle on Troglodon are now Priests, which is quite handy considering there’s a brand new prayer lore accompanying the new rules.*

Bite of Chotec is particularly handy if you want to give your opponent a nasty surprise in melee.

PRAYERS TO THE OLD ONES

Your Hero Phase

BITE OF CHOTEC (4)

The priest beseeches the sun god Chotec to imbue the weapons of the Seraphon with his blessing, causing them to release incinerating bursts of solar energy when they strike true.

Declare: Pick a friendly SERAPHON PRIEST to chant this prayer, pick a visible friendly SERAPHON unit wholly within 12" of them to be the target, then make a chanting roll of D6.

Effect: If the chanting roll was 8+, you can pick another eligible unit to be a second target. Until the start of your next hero phase, the targets’ melee weapons have Crit (2 Hits).

KEYWORDS: PRAYER, UNLIMITED

As is to be expected, the battletome also introduces a number of new Battle Formations, Heroic Traits, and Artefacts of Power for Seraphon players. The Crest of Chotec** is a great choice for those of you who love firing off celestial laser beams (and let’s face it, who doesn’t?).

TREASURES OF THE OLD ONES

Your Shooting Phase

CREST OF CHOTEC

This shimmering feathered headdress, inset with a brilliant carnelian gem, can loose an incinerating beam that burns with the heat of a star’s core.

Declare: Pick a point on the battlefield within 6" of this unit to be the target. Add 2" to the range for each asterism you have witnessed.

Effect: Draw a straight line between the target and the closest part on this unit’s base. Roll a D3 for each unit (friendly and enemy) that the line passes across. On a 2+, inflict an amount of mortal damage on that unit equal to the roll.

The new battletome is available for pre-order from Saturday. In the meantime, keep your eye on the heavens (or more specifically Warhammer Community) as later in the week we’ll be taking a look at some updated warscrolls for the Seraphon and their new Armies of Renown rules.

* Almost like it’s all been planned…
** Blimey, Chotec has been name dropped quite a lot. For those of you who aren’t in the knowtec, he is the Seraphon god of the sun and general representative of everything bright and burny.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: More Battle March armies from the Warhammer: The Old World team
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Get inspired by more forces for the smaller scale, fast-paced game mode.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
Earlier in the year, we showed off some incredible Battle March armies from the team behind Warhammer: The Old World. They’ve been busy painting more, and with the Tomb Kings of Khemri Battle March going up for pre-order tomorrow, now’s a great time to show them off.

Dominik – Warriors of Chaos

When planning this army, I knew I wanted to paint a force dedicated to Khorne, the Bloodied Hound as he’s called in Norsca. Inspired by classic Warhammer armies, I painted the army bright red with lots of gold trim. The bone-coloured helmets break this up and help to draw the eye to the focal point of the models.

With a Battle March army completed, I plan to expand the army with large units of Chaos Marauders and Marauder Horsemen, before finally adding a Chaos Dragon.

David – Warriors of Chaos

To paint the large areas of armour on my models, I started with a basecoat of Leadbelcher, over which I painted Black Templar Contrast paint to give them an oily, grimy feel, perfect for Warriors who’ve marched all the way from the Shard Lands to make war upon the Old World. For the fur coats and smaller details, I started by drybrushing on my base coats, over which I used a combination of Contrast paints and washes to add depth, before finally picking out the smaller details to tie everything together.

I’ve got plans to expand this army to 2,000 points or more, but unlike Dom I won’t be waiting to paint my Chaos Dragon – that’s the next model in my painting queue!

Dave – Grand Cathay

Inspired by Miao Ying sailing to the aid of the Old World from Fu Hung, the capital of Cathay's Southern Provinces, I imagined her brother, Li Dao, the Fire Dragon, sending a fleet of his own alongside hers.

As such, my Cathayans have been painted in reds and yellows, evoking their patron’s fiery spirit. The reds were basecoated Word Bearers Red and given a wash of Berserker Bloodshade with a Mephiston Red drybrush and highlight. The brighter yellows were used sparingly as spot colours, achieved with a Casandora Yellow wash over an Averland Sunset base, and highlighted with Yriel Yellow.

Having swapped the Battle Standard Bearer from the Core Set for an Astromancer to bring some magical support (they use Elementalism in games of Battle March, as is appropriate for a servant of the Fire Dragon!), I'm already planning my next units. My goal is to paint up a pair of Peasant Levy units as an alternative to the Grand Cannon, swapping heavy firepower for even more massed infantry.

Mark – Dwarfen Mountain Holds

With this army, my goal was to paint a solid core quickly, and then add to it later as new units are completed. With this in mind, I chose a simple paint scheme with not too many different colours. First I sprayed the models with Runelord Brass and washed them all with a 50/50 mix of Ratling Grime and Garaghak’s Sewer to pick out details. With a solid base colour for my models’ armour completed, I switched to painting five at a time, fixing the models to a strip of thick card and completing all five before moving on to the next batch.

I'm pleased with how the hand-painted banner designs came out. Little touches like this really make an army your own. I’m not sure what I’ll paint next and don’t really have a points limit in mind. I always paint the models I like the most, then write a muster list from what’s in my collection ahead of each game.

Christian – Beastmen Brayherds

For this army, I wanted to concentrate on models I love, but that would also be quick to paint. I already knew I wanted a strong contrast between model and base, so I opted for a red scheme with classic green basing.

The models were primed Chaos Black, then given a zenithal spray of White Scar. Over this I used mainly Contrast paints – Fyreslayer Flesh for the skin, Black Legion and Wyldwood for the fur, Gore-Grunta Fur and Snakebite Leather for the leather details, and Flesh Tearers Red for the red. The bases are more elaborate on the characters and elite units, but all of them feature fallen branches and tree trunks, represented by sticks and twigs I picked up whilst walking the dog. Details like these add volume to the bases and help to tell the story of a herd of Beastmen emerging from the depths of the forest.

If you like your games of fantasy football filled with madness, mayhem, and teeth, you’ll love the new Blood Bowl team. We hopped over to the Design Studio to get the lowdown on the new Squigs (and their Night Goblin assistants).

Tom: A never-before-seen team comes to Blood Bowl in the form of the Night Goblins. These wacky, unhinged Goblins have lingered in the background of the lore for a long time – Fanatics actually originate from Night Goblin ‘ingenuity’! Now they’re stepping into the limelight themselves – we’ve made sure it’s on a low light setting of course!

While regular Goblin teams have long run amok upon the field, Night Goblins bring their own brand of madness to the fore. Firstly, there are the Squigs. These bulbous, bouncing balls of hunger and rage are vicious opponents and diverse in their abilities. It’s not just typical Cave Squigs that you’ll have to face from Night Goblin teams, but also the speedy, bouncing Hoppers and frenzied wrecking balls that pull their Wranglers in every direction.

All this Squig action sounds too good to be true? Well, there is the tiny issue of Squig aggression to deal with. This is expressed through the new Squig Rage trait, which can result in your Squigs choosing to take a bite out of whoever is standing next to them – friend or foe – instead of immediately obeying you. Luckily, you have some tools to mitigate this!

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard rules
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Learn about the new options for the Kingdom of Bretonnia and Tomb Kings of Khemri.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
The imminent arrival of Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard brings new content for all players of Warhammer: the Old World, in particular the bold defenders of Bretonnia and the cadaverous servants of Nehekhara. To find out more about the rules contained within, we ventured into the Warhammer Studio in search of the writers.

JTY: Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard contains a wealth of new rules for Tomb Kings of Khemri and Kingdom of Bretonnia players alike, as well as four exciting new scenarios that allow players to recreate the key battles of the baron’s quest.

The first recreates the Bretonnians’ landing upon the ancient docks of Zandri and their attempt to escape that benighted city-port before the dead that populate it can gather. This is a Battle March scenario that the attackers (the Bretonnians) will find very challenging because every time they destroy an enemy unit, there is a chance an identical unit will arrive from reserve.

Dave: In the second scenario, the Bretonnians find themselves beset from all sides by Undead monstrosities as they cross the empty deserts of the Land of the Dead. The third recreates Sir Varo’s flight from Numas as he attempts to escape the clutches of the horror he has awakened.

In the final scenario, the Tomb Kings come face to face with a vast horde of Orcs and Goblins as they pursue their quarry across the Badlands. As the two armies approach one another, Sir Varo leads his knights in a glorious charge against the Undead, hoping to strike a deadly blow against the evil king that leads them and restore honour to his quest, making for a unique three-player scenario.

JTY: For Tomb Kings of Khemri players, the new content comes in the form of Dynastic Rulers and Dynastic Armies. This allows players to choose to have their army represent one of the powerful dynasties that once ruled the Great Land.

These rules give the characters that lead the army upgrades that suit the style of warfare they mastered in life. Monarchs of Nehekhara belonging to the first dynasty, which originated from Khemri, for example, have improved Weapon Skill and Initiative to reflect their martial prowess. Those belonging to the third dynasty, from Zandri, must be mounted on Skeleton Chariots, but are such skilled charioteers that they can re-roll failed dangerous terrain tests and improve the AP of their Impact Hits by 1.

Khemri – The First Dynasty

In life, as they are in death, the rulers of Nehekhara’s first and greatest city were renowned as fine and noble warriors. They were also fiercely proud, often preferring to vanquish enemies by their own hand rather than allow heralds to fight their duels.

Tomb Kings and Tomb Princes belonging to the First Dynasty have a +1 modifier to their Weapon Skill and Initiative characteristics, as well as a +1 modifier to the Armour Piercing characteristic of any non-magical weapons they wield. However, a Monarch of Nehekhara that belongs to the First Dynasty cannot decline a challenge.

Zandri – The Third Dynasty

Famed not only for its bustling docks and its construction of the vast ocean-going fleets that allowed Nehekhara to rule the waves in ancient times, Zandri also produced some of the Great Land’s finest chariots and charioteers. The noble charioteers of Zandri would spend years honing their skills in races run upon the parade grounds of sprawling palaces and temples, and even through the bustling streets of their cities. Their mastery was not limited to entertainment however, for they were also deadly warriors, able and eager to take to the battlefield when the need arose.

Tomb Kings, Tomb Princes and Royal Heralds belonging to the Third Dynasty that are mounted on Skeleton Chariots gain the First Charge special rule, and may re-roll any rolls of a 1 made when making a Dangerous Terrain test. In addition, any Impact Hits caused by these characters’ chariots have an Armour Piercing characteristic of -1.

There are similar upgrades for units as well, with those that benefit depending upon which dynasty you choose to represent. It’s a lot of fun figuring out how best to theme a Tomb Kings of Khemri army in order to make the most of each dynasty’s quirks!

Dave: For the Kingdom of Bretonnia, there’s a Questing Host Army of Infamy, inspired by Lord Carrard and his bold quest into the heart of Nehekhara. Anyone using this Army of Infamy can field a unit or two of Questing Knights amongst their Core choices, but it’s the way the army interacts with Pledges of Honour that make this army really exciting.

These are new upgrades available to knightly units and characters. In most armies, only models with the Questing Vow can swear a Pledge of Honour. But in a Questing Host, all models with a Knightly Vow can!

Pledges of Honour represent the types of pledge the knights of Bretonnia often swear on the eve of battle – noble boasts and chivalrous promises made to the Lady of the Lake. Models that fulfil their pledges during the battle gain Victory Point bonuses at its end. For example, a character that has sworn the Pledge of Conquest earns 50 VP if they are within the enemy’s deployment zone at the end of the battle. A unit that has sworn the Pledge of Protection earns 50 VP if it controls an objective when the battle ends.

Pledge Of Conquest

“By my hand, evil shall be vanquished and the lands it has conquered will be reclaimed.”

Should the character that swore this noble pledge be within your opponent’s deployment zone at the end of the battle, you win a bonus of 50 Victory Points.

Pledge Of Protection

“By our efforts the field will be won, and the enemy will be driven into the wilderness.”

0-1 per Army. If the unit that swore this knightly pledge is controlling an objective (such as a treasure trove, a baggage train, a special feature, a battlefield quarter, etc.) at the end of the battle, you win a bonus of 50 Victory Points.

As a long-time Bretonnia player, I’ve always said that chivalry is its own reward, but now there’s an actual reward – Victory Points!

Thanks, folks! The new Arcane Journal is available to pre-order on Saturday, along with a veritable legion of Tomb Kings of Khemri miniatures. In the meantime, learn more about the lore of the supplement.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Learn about the background of the Bretonnian baron’s fateful quest.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
The latest Arcane Journal, The Doom of Lord Carrard, will be available to pre-order this weekend. To find out more, we undertook our own quest into the depths of the Warhammer studio to speak to the designers about the lore of the latest supplement.

JTY: Since the release of Warhammer: The Old World, we’ve been following the events of Settra the Imperishable’s war against the Old World. We’ve seen his armies advance through the Border Princes and navigate the peaks and valleys of the Vaults en route to the borders of Bretonnia. We’ve even seen what happens when an ancient Liche Priest leads an army of the Undead into the depths of Athel Loren. But what we haven’t covered in much detail is what caused all this turmoil in the first place.

In Arcane Journal – the Doom of Lord Carrard we decided to address this. We wanted to explore the charnel realm of Nehekhara in greater detail, and we felt Lord Carrard’s quest allowed us to do just that.

Much of the narrative is told from the perspective of the Bretonnians, giving us a relatable lens through which to view the horrors of the Land of the Dead. This allowed us to introduce Lord Carrard himself, a baron from the realm of Brionne, and establish his relationship with Sir Lothar of Kasos Rock, once a noble knight of Carrard’s court but now an outcast dwelling in the Border Princes.

It is the arrival of a messenger from Sir Lothar that sets in motion the events that are to follow. Bringing the grim forebodings from Sir Lothar’s court, the messenger warns of a great evil stirring in the Land of the Dead and implores Lord Carrard for his aid in vanquishing it. Rather than muster armies on the strength of vague portents, the baron elects to undertake a quest, riding in the company of his closest companions to the court of his former friend.

The next part of the story is told through the recollections of Sir Varo, one of the few to return and bring word of Lord Carrard’s fate, and of the evil that has been awakened in the Land of the Dead. Through Varo we learn of the Bretonnians’ journey to the accursed city of Zandri, from where we explore Nehekhara itself, coming face to face with the horrors of the Land of the Dead as the bold knights cross the deserts and battle the undead horrors placed before them. Accompanied by a wealth of stunning new art, this tale casts a whole new light upon this accursed realm, giving the reader a sense of the scale of the civilisation that once ruled the deserts of the Great Land, and the horrors a traveller might encounter in deserts haunted by looming horrors beneath skies shrouded behind impregnable dust storms.

But that’s not all. Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard also examines ancient Nehekhara, in particular the major cities of that once-vibrant land, and the royal dynasties that once ruled over them. Delving into such ancient history was a fun challenge, and reading about the cities and dynasties of the Land of the Dead will hopefully inspire readers. There are lots of ideas here for theming your own collections of Tomb Kings of Khemri to reflect the armies of a particular city or monarch.

It’s always fun to explore the World of Legend, and shining a light on the events that led to Settra's climactic invasion was especially enjoyable. This was a story we were keen to tell, and we can’t wait to see how it will inspire readers!

Thanks, JTY! The new Arcane Journal is available for pre-order from Saturday, along with a wealth of reinforcements for the Tomb Kings of Khemri in the form of Skeleton Warriors, Skeleton Archers, Horsemen and Horse Archers, and Skeleton Chariots. Join us later in the week when we’ll be learning more about the rules in the Arcane Journal.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: New rules revealed for narrative-driven action in the Mortal Realms.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
A new Path to Glory expansion is coming for Warhammer Age of Sigmar. Get ready to head to Chamon, the Realm of Metal, to reclaim a lost hold of the Khazalid empire.

Karak Vanggaz was once the pride of the ancient Khazalid empire. Betrayed from within, its duardin rulers were driven out and the once-mighty stronghold fell into ruin. Now, the throngs of the Khazalites have returned, and subterranean halls long abandoned echo to the sound of clashing blades as warring factions vie for control of hidden riches in this latest narrative supplement for Path to Glory.

The Grymmpeaks is the newest story-driven battlepack for Path to Glory, giving Warhammer Age of Sigmar players access to a whole host of tools for creating thematic campaigns set within the treacherous confines of a lost duardin mine.

A new narrative sets the stage, charting the expedition of a Khazalite Thrynn to reclaim his ancestral birthright. Unbeknownst to him, a force of the Helsmiths of Hashut – the accursed duardin responsible for the original treachery which brought Karak Vanggaz into ruin – have their avaricious eyes set on claiming its ancient treasures for their infernal master.

As with previous battlepacks, Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks provides rules for bespoke Paths your units can undertake. Among these, and in honour of the distinctly duardin setting, is the Path of the Armourer, allowing your Heroes to harness the power of Chamonite to forge inviolable armour for them and their allies.

There are new rules for fighting in the lightless depths beneath the mountains, including opportunities to breach pillars and walls so your force can forge a clear path forward. Meanwhile, centuries of neglect and ruin have turned the subterranean confines of Karak Vanggaz into a health and safety nightmare. The new battlepack contains rules representing the myriad underground hazards that await your forces.

Although Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks focuses its narrative on Khazalite Holds vs Helsmiths of Hashut, the rules in the battlepack are designed to be used by any faction. In the wake of the Hour of Ruin, perhaps a group of enterprising Skaven have sniffed out an opportunity to move in? What if the spirits of the old inhabitants never left? Path to Glory allows you to tell your own story.

Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks will also be available as a special Warlord Edition. This comes packed with extra tools to help forge your Path to Glory campaign, including a deck of reference cards for traits, artifacts and hazards and a Chamonite Ore Point dial, helping you track gathered resources throughout the course of a game.

Both versions will be available to pre-order soon. Keep your eyes peeled on Warhammer Community as we’ll be taking a closer look at the rules from the book, and in the meantime explore the new Khazalite Holds range and start planning your expedition to reclaim Karak Vanggaz.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Meet the Khazalite Ancestor Gods
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Who exactly are the duardin swearing oaths to?
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
The Ancestor Gods are a pretty big deal in Khazalite culture, showing up in both their army rules and prayer lores – but before you start swearing oaths or chanting prayers, make sure you know exactly who you’re beseeching for aid.

The duardin of the Khazalite Holds believe their eight gods were once mortals, and though some are older than others, all hold equal veneration in the hearts of honest, goodly Khazalites. All but one…

Grungni – The Father God

Grungni is the most respected of all the Ancestor Gods, renowned for his great deeds, including forging lightning for Sigmar himself. The Khazalites understand that Grungni wants to see their scattered clans united, based on his mantra that the duardins’ path will only hold if it is forged through unity.

Valaya – The Mother Goddess

A symbol of fortitude and healing, fortress builders honour her as protector of duardin holdings, and brewers revere her as the patron of all ales. In ancient days, her shield spared Karak Thryngaz from immolation, and cleansed the waters of Strufsson’s Tarn, saving its breweries.

Gazul – The God of the Underworld

The Stonebeard guides the dead on their final journey to his Gate, and through his runic mastery their souls are kept safe from the clutches of Nagash. His watch is endless, standing vigil against quiet undead and horrors of Chaos alike.

Grimnir – The God of the Axe and Battle

Known as the Fearless, Grimnir represents the warrior spirit of the duardin. The Fyreslayers believe that, despite falling in battle against the godbeast Vulcatrix, some part of his spirit endures.

Grombrindal – The White Dwarf

Old Whitebeard, the Wanderer – there isn’t a duardin who doesn’t know the legends of Grombrindal. An ever-roaming wayfarer and rememberer of places, Grombrindal guides the duardin in their search for lost karaks.

Thorgrim – The Grudgebearer

Stern as iron, Thorgrim remembers every ill deed and wrong perpetrated against the duardin, adding them to 

his Great Library of Grudges. He embodies the vengeful side of the duardin, hoarding the grudges of an entire race so that they do not consume their souls.

Inghilde – The Delver

The youngest of the pantheon, Inghilde’s intrepid spirit inspires the duardin to prospect and mine deep beneath the earth’s surface. She is the patron goddess of miners and stonesmiths, and, like Grombrindal, represents the pioneering spirit of the duardin – him above ground and her below.

Hashut – The Fallen God

Shorn from the pantheon, his statues rubble and his name a curse, Hashut is the fallen God who brings shame to all duardin. When any hope of redemption was lost, it was Valaya who struck him down.

Find out more about the Ancestor Gods, and the wider Khazalite Holds, when their battletome goes up for pre-order this Saturday, alongside their new miniatures.

In the fourth installment of the legendary Warhammer 40,000 real-time strategy game series, you can take control of four factions – the Space Marines of the Blood Ravens and Dark Angels, Orks, Necrons, and Adeptus Mechanicus – across four campaigns comprising more than 70 thrilling missions.


In addition to the campaigns, there’s a Skirmish mode, with dozens of customisable settings, four game types, and support for up to five AI opponents, where you can hone your skills before taking the battle online across 30 multiplayer maps.

The Last Stand

Fan-favourite co-op survival mode The Last Stand is back, where you and two allies must hold the line against relentless waves of enemies. Choose from five heroes and assemble your strike force of companion units, bringing new layers of strategic depth to every run.

Whichever mode you like to play, the enhanced Painter tool means you can make every army your own. Choose from dozens of presets or create your own schemes with choices of colours, decals, and wargear – for the first time, you have complete creative control to paint your units’ armour and equipment piece-by-piece.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is due for release on 3 December 2026, but if you can’t wait until then, the Commander Edition gives players early access three days ahead of the main release. Pre-order either edition now to get a 10% discount, and prepare to begin the fight for Kronus anew.
